newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: BOXING-ESPINOSA KEEPS WBC CROWN AFTER HEAD BUTT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-ESPINOSA KEEPS WBC CROWN AFTER HEAD BUTT.

text.p: Filipino Luisito Espinosa, bleeding from cuts over both eyes, retained his World Boxing Council (WBC) featherweight crown on Saturday when the referee stopped his fight with Mexico's Manuel Medina after the champion suffered a head butt in the eighth round.

Espinosa, 29, was leading on the scorecards of the three ring judges when American referee Jan Nagy halted the bout at one minute 22 seconds of the eighth round of the scheduled 12-round contest at Manila's Rizal Park.
Espinosa turned away from the Mexican after a collision of heads and Nagy waived the fight over after the ring physician examined a one-inch gash over the champion's right eye.

Espinosa also bled from a cut over the left eye in the seventh round after an exchange with Medina, who was the aggressor throughout the fight before 20,000 fans, including Philippine President Fidel Ramos.
Nagy ruled the fight a "technical decision" for Espinosa because he was ahead on points when the accidental butt occurred.
Judges from the United States and Japan both had Espinosa ahead 78-73 while another American judge had Espinosa leading 77-75 when the fight was stopped.

But the contest appeared much closer than the cards indicated as the 29-year old Mexican kept beating Espinosa to the punch, jarring him with combinations to the face and punishing the Filipino with body blows in the first three rounds.
Espinosa shook Medina several times but the Mexican kept coming back, scoring with right straights to Espinosa's face.
It was Espinosa's fourth defence of the title he wrested from Medina in their first meeting in Tokyo in December 1995.
